supporter: I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us. 
seeker: How did your dog come with the house?
supporter: Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.
supporter: I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.
seeker: I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2
seeker: Thank you. that means a lot
seeker: We both had dogs when we met.
supporter: So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol
supporter: I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it! 
seeker: They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes
supporter: I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.
supporter: I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.
seeker: Thanks. Another person who has pets helps
seeker: They understand
supporter: I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.
supporter: I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog. 
seeker: Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.
supporter: Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed. 
seeker: That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.
supporter: I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D
seeker: You too. Thanks so much. bye

seeker: I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also
supporter: I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious? 
seeker: I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.
supporter: Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?
seeker: Like meditation?
seeker: What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?
supporter: Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. Slowly breathe in for a count of 5, then slowly exhale for a count of 5. Repeat this process for approximately 10 minute. It will help your stress levels and help regulate your heart rate!
seeker: Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?
supporter: I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.
seeker: ok I can try it I guess
seeker: thanks for that tip
supporter: No problem. I hope this gives you some relief! Stay strong!
seeker: yeah, thanks. same to you
supporter: My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.
seeker: That's helpful. Thanks.
supporter: No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.
seeker: Thanks. You too

Yes, I sometimes feel guilty and then don't want to face the music, but actually the best thing to do is recognize you are NOT the first person she knows that got behind. So she is surely experienced with people who need some encouragement. She is the BEST person to go to, actually.
That sounds like a good idea regarding putting it down on paper.

It has always helped me. For example, you can break it down into 4 weeks, then each week write your goals -- maybe put call Advisor or go stop by every week, but I would put that first for the first week.

Then as you check off items, you will see you are moving, even if at a snail's pace, you are moving, and that always encourages me. Sometimes I do not realize how much I AM doing, until I see it on paper. Paper doesn't lie, but my emotions sometimes cloud my thinking.
My other problem is that I'm a perfectionist. I tend to over-analyze and get bogged down, especially when doing research.
Another idea is rewards, when you finish one goal, perhaps put a reward for yourself,  a yogurt with sprinkles or something like that

That is why a time line is good. For example, you make a goal that you will work on your reference and citation page for one hour, after that, you are DONE, If you have time at the end, you can revisit it. The hour is my suggestion, you make your own. lol THAT way, you don't get caught going on and on for 6 hours to make it perfect. One hour is reasonable.
That definitely sounds reasonable. Putting micro deadlines in might be what I need to do to keep me focused.

I do this with EVERYTHING in life because I tend to go on and on too focused and lose track of everything. lol For example, I clean each room for 15 minutes a week. If it needs more, I do more, but I set the timer and you would be surprised how well that works, otherwise, I will spend all my time perfecting one room and the rest is a mess.

My advisor is a tough woman, I'm not going to beat around the bush. She tends to make everything miserable.

supporter: Courage is making the best choice for yourself, even when it's hard. You’ve shown strength in so many ways already.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. I guess hearing it from someone else makes it feel more valid.
supporter: Absolutely. Remember, asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
seeker: I’ll try to remember that. I really appreciate you listening.
supporter: I'm always here to listen, John. You're doing the best you can, and that’s enough.
